newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent stagnates, seen stifled by holiday torpo.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent stagnates, seen stifled by holiday torpo.

text.p: IPE Brent futures stagnated in a moribund market on Friday as the continued absence of many European players subdued trade, traders said.
June IPE Brent was three cents higher at $18.32 a barrel at 1017 GMT, while May gas oil was $2.00 lower at $169.00 a tonne.
"It's rangebound. Volumes are thin. We won't see anything until the States comes in later on," said one trader.
Traders said many European players appeared to have extended Thursday's holiday into the weekend, while London-based players appeared to winding down ahead of Britain's bank holiday on Monday.
On the technical front, traders said closure of the $18.62/77 downside gap remained June Brent's key upside target.
Some viewed its prolonged failure to fill the gap as an increasingly bearish sign.
Support for June was seen around the $18.20 level in line with a hub of price activity over the past two weeks. Below there recent lows at $17.81 and $17.61 were seen beckoning.

Traders attributed gas oil's losses to some minor profit-taking. Key support for the May contract was pegged around $169.00/50 in line with a downside gap between April 29 and 30. - Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
